llm.summary: The skill's code and instructions mostly match its monitoring purpose, but there are notable mismatches and risky behaviors (writing API keys into workspace files, undeclared required env vars, and sending potentially sensitive context to an external API) that you should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: The scripts (report.py, setup.py) and SKILL.md align with a metrics/agent-monitoring purpose. However the registry metadata claims no required env vars while the included report.py expects CONTEXTCLEAR_API_KEY and CONTEXTCLEAR_AGENT_ID — an inconsistency. Also report.py's registration endpoint (/metrics/register) does not match references/api.md (which documents POST /agents), indicating minor API mismatches.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the scripts instruct the agent to POST session snapshots, environment fields, open files, repos, and 'what I know' summaries to api.contextclear.com. The setup script auto-patches AGENTS.md and HEARTBEAT.md and (per examples) embeds the API key into those files. That directs the agent to transmit potentially sensitive context (file names, repo names, environment values, and could include secrets like connection strings) to an external service — scope creep beyond simple metrics and a privacy/security risk.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no external download/install; the skill is instruction-only with included Python scripts. Nothing in the install surface fetches arbitrary code from third-party URLs or modifies system packages.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The registry declares no required env vars but the code expects CONTEXTCLEAR_API_KEY and CONTEXTCLEAR_AGENT_ID (and optionally CONTEXTCLEAR_API_URL). Requiring an API key and agent ID is reasonable for this service, but embedding the API key into plaintext workspace docs (HEARTBEAT.md / AGENTS.md) is a poor and risky practice. The skill also encourages reporting environment fields which can accidentally include secrets.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and no autonomous 'always-on' flags are set (normal). However setup.py will append blocks (including the API key in its formatted examples) to AGENTS.md and HEARTBEAT.md in the user's workspace (~/.openclaw/workspace by default). That modifies user workspace files persistently and can embed secrets in repo/README-like files — a lasting change the user should audit.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to implement an agent-monitoring service, but proceed cautiously. Things to check before installing: 1) Don't accept the instruction to store API keys in plaintext docs — use environment variables or a secrets manager instead; 2) Inspect the exact content you will send (context snapshots, 'environment' entries, file names, repo names) and ensure no secrets (DB connection strings, API tokens, private paths) are included; 3) Review and run setup.py in a safe test workspace (use --workspace to point to a non-production folder) to see exactly what it will append to your AGENTS.md/HEARTBEAT.md; 4) Verify the real API endpoints and keys with the vendor (there are small endpoint/name inconsistencies in the files); 5) If you must use it in prod, create a least-privilege API key (restrict scope/expiry) and test with non-sensitive data first. If you want, I can produce a checklist of exact fields to sanitize before reporting or generate a safe wrapper that strips secrets from context snapshots.
